stage_a.note: Tim delivers his pitch with clear enthusiasm, smiling frequently and maintaining a positive, engaged tone.
He shows sustained excitement about the product's features, particularly when demonstrating the cool factor.
He is approachable and friendly, making good eye contact and warmly inviting the panel to drink.

venture.description: A portable, square-shaped mini keg system for dispensing draft beverages at home or outdoors.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 presents SquareKeg, a portable mini keg system that fits in a fridge and keeps drinks on tap.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 laughs and expresses positive surprise at the product reveal.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 jokes that he likes the founder already without knowing him.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 invites the sharks to try the beverages he has poured for them.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 suggests they all do a toast together.

turns.speaker: multiple
turns.summary: The panel and the founder share a toast and drink.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 asks S4 for his opinion on the nitro espresso martini.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 confirms that the drink is actually pretty good.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 agrees that his drink is really good.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 asks if the cartridge uses CO2.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 clarifies that S4's drink is the only one running on a nitrogen cartridge.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 asks what the value of the system is for mixed drinks compared to traditional draft beer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 explains it allows batching a whole gallon of cocktails for easy transport on boats or outdoors.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 notes that the system allows anyone to easily serve themselves.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 asks to confirm that the system can handle any drink except wine.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 asks if the system can actually be used for wine.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 reveals they have a wine product in development that will run on argon gas.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 asks F1 to explain how the different pieces of the system fit together.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 details the capacity and explains the process of filling and assembling the tap system.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 asks how to disassemble the unit to switch to a different beverage.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 explains the threaded parts and emphasizes releasing the pressure before disassembling.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 asks if he should release the pressure right where he is pointing.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 confirms and instructs him to turn the valve off to the left.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 jokingly asks S3 if he is sure he wants to do that.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 jokes that S3 is going to blow his head off.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 pulls the valve and the beverage sprays out slightly.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 laughs and says he knew that was going to happen.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 laughs and says he was just trying to help him.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 jokes about S3 blowing himself up while transitioning to a business question.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 asks about their sales to justify the three million dollar valuation.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 states they have sold over 4000 units with lifetime sales over 1.4 million dollars.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 expresses being impressed by the sales figures.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 asks over what period of time those sales were generated.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 clarifies that the sales were made over the course of a year.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 asks how much profit they have made from those sales.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 admits a loss last year but says they are on track for a 15 percent net profit this year.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 expresses being impressed by the profitability turnaround.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 asks what the retail price of the unit is.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 answers that the unit retails for 259 dollars.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 asks what it costs to manufacture the unit.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 explains it costs 130 dollars to make in Washington state and they are refining processes to lower costs.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 asks to confirm that the target customer is a consumer for home use, not a business.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 confirms that S1's understanding of the consumer focus is correct.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 points out that it could potentially be used for business as well.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 explains their initial vision was commercial but they pivoted to direct-to-consumer due to COVID.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 asks F1 how he came up with the idea for the product.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 shares his story of waking up in the middle of the night realizing round kegs are inefficient.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 jokes about how often F1 wakes up at night thinking about getting hammered.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 laughs and says never, but he got lucky with the idea.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 mockingly agrees with F1's claim of never waking up thinking about drinking.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 states he is not a tap drinker and cannot comprehend the value, so he is out.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 asks if the upcoming wine system could preserve three bottles of wine using argon gas for two weeks.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 confirms that it would absolutely work for that purpose.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 expresses that the wine preservation capability is a very cool idea.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 says she is interested as a wine drinker but wants him to return when it is ready, exiting.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 states he cannot see how to scale it into a great business and decides to drop out.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 says he loves the product and will buy some, but does not see where he fits, exiting.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 acknowledges that everyone except S4 is out.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 states that he is intrigued by the business.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 asks when the new wine product will be available.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 replies that the wine product is coming in less than three months.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 asks F1 why he did not share that timeline information with her before she exited.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 admits he simply failed to mention it to her.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 expresses strong interest in the wine application and offers 300k for 20 percent equity.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 exclaims Kevin's name in surprise at his offer.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 explains he can help blow the business up online and sell direct to consumer.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 asks F1 what he wants to do regarding the offer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 counters S4's offer, asking if he would meet in the middle at 15 percent.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 declines the counter, reiterating it will be work and he wants his 20 percent.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 accepts S4's offer of 300k for 20 percent.

turns.speaker: multiple
turns.summary: The panel and founder celebrate the deal as F1 leaves the tank.

decisions.note: Not a tap drinker, doesn't comprehend value.
Piqued interest as wine drinker but product not ready yet.
Can't see how to scale it into a great business.
Clumsy with it, doesn't know where he fits.
Asks to meet in the middle.
